author: ViTaLDRuG
text:
I am having really hard time understanding how Salivan marks Flag
limits. What is taught in RTM is, that if a important level is broken
and price hits a TG, then the kink created after breaking that important
 level, is a FL ( not as simple as that, but as a brief explanation.. )

Salivan simply marks the FLs, by stating if they hold price up or down.
He doesnt often mention the important level broken. I am wondering if
anyone can explain how he marks the FLs. I know it is his own way of

author: staurum
text:
FL can be found in Left Shoulder, R/S, PreCP, a break into CP.
Previously we are taught FL established on S/R. Sali does mark the FLs
on S/R, but he just picks the obvious ones that hold price. Swap FLs are
 also obvious.

On that GU chart,

FL1 = a break of 2May1996 low.

FL 2 = swap to FL1

FL 3 = swap to his "OrFL"

FL 4 = break of 97 Oct high, resulting in a very BIG FL.

FL 5 = self explanatory

FL 6 = break of 1992 high.

FL 7 = swap to FL6

FL 8 - swap to FL3 and also break of the big FL4.

text:
[Part 2]

Another is from Whenever (thanks to Whenever):
 readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/jou...ions?start=150#43381

Then comes RDK with his dilemma:Rdk123 wrote: Thanks for your reply, unfortunately the question is still not answered.

I'll break it down even more, so, a Flag limit is a DBD or RBR, does the
 BASE have to engulf the S/R? Because a wick coming close to engulfing
is not an engulf, do you see where I'm coming from?

I have no problem in identifying the DBD or RBR, this is not the
problem. My question is, does the first drop or rally in a DBD or RBD
have to engulf the s/r?

This has come about through a lot of investigation in to the FL's that work and don't work. This isn't day one for me.

Here is one of the diagrams from a previous post again, which would you
say is the FL in the context of this diagram with no other factors? A or
 B?

To me, B signifies the end of momentum and the decision to engulf the
s/r, hence it is the FL Limit, the last line of defense protecting entry
 to the FLAG. A is just the first time back, the key decision has
already been made, A is just an FTR unless it becomes the decision to
engulf some base or s/r above (as per the last scenario in my last
post).

I'd be interest to see your take on this and why you would think A might
 be more important that B. Think of it this way, A is a reaction to B,
so which is more important? Where are the orders? where did the
imbalance originate?

Cheers,

Robbie

Which was then attended by Rcmacf:rcmacf
 wrote: The flag limit is the feature which defines the flag. As Robbie
 stated previously, where the flag goes to beyond the limit is not
relevant. (Well, it is relevant in so much as where the areas of S/D are
 within the flag - as this is where price will react on return, once the
 flag limit is broken.

So, the diagram you've posted above does not show the flag limit, it
shows where the flag was (maybe) broken. The full story would be
something like I've marked here, where the blue box is the flag limit,
defined by the points noted in the green circles ( the FL as the
abbreviation). So, what's marked as B is the Decision Point (DP) to
break the flag and A is the FTR created after that break.

What I see is that the FTR was the price point the ITs used to be aiming
 for in the past, and would FO to the DP (B) but nowadays, they aim for
B, and what was once the FO zone, has become the new target.

Now, before going to Sali's findings about FL. Let me put Jurij's post here which may be relevant to the above issue.Jurij wrote: I see that the DP concept causes so much confusion.

Sometimes price respects the DP sometimes not.

Then the always recurring question, does an eng have to eng the DP too?

But think about DP, what is really a DP?

This is my view on it:

This is what we see

This is in terms of orders

There's no DP, only order flow and new transactions (FL).

Again just my understanding

text:

Sali's understanding about FL is found in his FOF article (
 readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/jou...-war?start=925#60487

 readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/jou...rnal?start=900#56379

that's why the (S/R)s always find value when a FL create not with out
FL. the chart is full of S/R but our chart is not covered by a lot of
FL.
 and again the reason is clear you can prove it in terms of OF for your
self . when the transaction of orders executed then balance in base of a
 Flag create and this balance still valid till an other imbalance start
and ENG prior balance so that now we need an opposite transaction of OF
to be execute.

if we can understand why do FLs create and what is their obligation in
price structure in terms of OF then i think it's easy to find them in
two confirmation :

1.

An FTR that hold price up or down is FL(BUFL,BEFL)

2.

FL is a kind of FTR that ENGULF an other FL.

hope it helps you

best

Salivan

So the most recent FL concept (which leads me to Sali's concept) makes
me look at an engulf of a FL which held price up/down and its resulting
FL (basically a swap FL). Sometimes it connects, but sometimes it drives
 me away from the very first FL concept, i.e. a break of significant S/R
 [swing high/low].

I can understand that Sali's FL concept requires confirmation (held
price and a swap to another FL). However seems like these two concepts,
to me at least personally, have created a confusion of FL markings while
 i'm trying to study PAZ and scales.

I remember reading one part of FL homework post where someone asked
whether or not a FTR needs a confirmation to hold price in order to
validate it as FL, and the answer is no. However, Sali used confirmation
 of "held price" to validate a FL.

Furthermore, after watching LiteCourse video 2 (where to look PA), I've
noted that : "FL can be found in Left Shoulder, R/S, PreCP, a break into
 CP. Previously we are taught FL established on S/R. Sali does mark the
FLs on S/R, but he just picks the obvious ones that hold price."

Now going into study of PAZ, we are taught that price moves from PAZ to
PAZ and FLs are their delimiters, therefore price moves from FL to FL. I
 found some difficulties when determining PAZ when marking FLs in a
chart are based on different concepts. I'm not sure if they are
different, or I wonder if Sali's FL concept is actually an advanced, or
extended, study of the basic FL concept (i.e. engulf of S/R, swing
high/low). Furthermore, the LiteCourse video no.2 adds FL markings on
the chart.

In the meantime, let's pretend that the above is solved: When setting
targets. From the Lite Course videos, IF explained that our target
(depending on scale) is to be set at the S/R of the FL. In other words,
once price touched its targeted FL's S/R box, then we can say Price Has
Met its TG. However, Sali extend his study on targets (ref:
 readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/hom...its?start=1000#54708
) and found that price's target is the QM level inside the targeted FL
(Sali, please correct me if i'm wrong). Did i doubt this? no.. he's
given many examples, and this (
 readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/hom...mits?start=975#54527
) is an excellent one.

I hope i'm not confusing myself here, let alone anyoneelse. Sali, based
on the above, you can imagine me marking lots and lots of FLs from
different concepts (hence PAZs). too many markings will just paralyze me
 trying to find engulfs to trade. Could you please help direct me. my
brain seems to have stuck here. By the way, I AM Very happy to see you
back on

(Side note: still at work. when i got home to find some messy charts i
talked about, i'll upload it here if u dont mind. the reason is i've
been trying to find some rules on PAZ for my own trading.)

Cheers,
